purpose: Private M2 secret generation and bearer-header authentication helper; no HTTP route, persistent issuer, deployment or performance benchmark.

beforeAfter.before: Code inspection: the baseline has project-bound PostgreSQL lookup but no hosted/auth secret/header helper. No deployed HTTP authentication service or old-version timing benchmark exists.
beforeAfter.after: The runnable provider-free example prints authorized for reading its own project, forbidden for ingest with a read-only key and for another project, and unauthenticated after revocation. The separate real-database test uses a generated secret against the restricted SQL lookup and observes membership downgrade/revocation.

requiredCommitGate: Exact staged-tree quality:record, quality:review and quality:verify must pass before commit; the ledger stores raw local command logs under the worktree Git directory.
limitations: The trusted production lookup adapter must bind the digest to resolve_api_credential using the restricted login and impose query timeouts; no adapter is shipped by this helper.
HTTP adapters must reject duplicate raw Authorization headers before framework normalization; the helper rejects array/comma representations but cannot detect a discarded duplicate.
No HTTP endpoint, TLS/rate limits, browser sessions, persistent credential issuer/rotation/audit, upload or worker is implemented here.
Secrets are returned to trusted issuer code, not automatically persisted or made one-time; that lifecycle remains future work. Never log token/digest/header/returned secret object.
Every allowed request needs a fresh trusted lookup and operation check. Revocation does not cancel work authorized before a database statement snapshot.
M2 stays open. Portable exports/schema/dependencies and offline operation are unchanged. Publishing/deployment remain separately authorized.
This record contains local pre-PR results. Current-head raw CI is verified and recorded on the PR before merge, with revisions identified explicitly.
